content.value_statement: Event-sourced systems need fast read models that stay consistent with event streams. This skill provides projection patterns for CQRS queries, dashboards, search, and reporting.
actual_capabilities: Explains live, catchup, persistent, and inline projection types.
Provides Python templates for projection base classes and checkpointed projectors.
Shows order summary read models using parameterized SQL updates.
Demonstrates Elasticsearch search indexing from product events.
Covers aggregate reporting and multi-table projection transactions.
Lists practical practices for idempotency, checkpoints, lag monitoring, and rebuilds.
limitations: Examples are templates and require adaptation to your event store and schema.
The skill does not include runnable tests or migration files.
Error handling, backpressure, and retry policies are described only at a high level.
It assumes familiarity with CQRS, async Python, SQL, and event-sourced architecture.

use_cases.title: Design CQRS Read Models
use_cases.description: Create read-side tables that answer product, order, or customer queries without loading full event streams.

use_cases.title: Build Operational Dashboards
use_cases.description: Aggregate event data into daily sales, activity, and status views for monitoring and reporting.

use_cases.title: Plan Projection Rebuilds
use_cases.description: Use checkpoints and catchup processing to rebuild materialized views after schema changes or failures.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Projection
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new read model.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a basic projection for my event-sourced system. My events are [events], and my query need is [query].

prompt_templates.title: Map Events to a Read Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to map these event types to a read model: [event list]. Include fields, handlers, and checkpointing guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Search Projection
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced search indexing from event streams.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a search projection for [domain]. Include indexing events, update events, deletes, and rebuild considerations.

prompt_templates.title: Review Projection Architecture
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced assessment of an existing projection system.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my projection architecture. Focus on idempotency, ordering, transaction boundaries, lag monitoring, and rebuild strategy.

output_examples.input: Design a projection for order summaries from order events.
output_examples.output: A read-model plan with handled events, table fields, update rules, checkpoint strategy, and rebuild notes.

output_examples.input: Create a projection for product search.
output_examples.output: A search-indexing design that covers product creation, updates, price changes, deletes, and index rebuild flow.

output_examples.input: Review a daily sales projection for reporting.
output_examples.output: A concise review of aggregation logic, idempotency risks, refund handling, checkpoint recovery, and monitoring needs.

best_practices: Keep each projection focused on one query model or reporting need.
Store checkpoints and design every handler to be safe during replay.
Use transactions when one event updates multiple read-model tables.
anti_patterns: Do not couple projections so one read model depends on another.
Do not ignore event ordering when rebuilding or catching up projections.
Do not over-normalize read models when denormalized tables serve queries better.

faq.question: What problem does this skill solve?
faq.answer: It helps design read models and projections for CQRS and event-sourced systems.

faq.question: Does it generate production-ready code?
faq.answer: It provides templates and architecture guidance. You must adapt them to your schemas, infrastructure, and reliability requirements.

faq.question: Can it help with Elasticsearch projections?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a product search projection pattern that covers indexing, updates, price changes, and deletion.

faq.question: Does it cover projection rebuilds?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains catchup processing, checkpoints, and replay-safe design for read-model reconstruction.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should I verify before using the templates?
faq.answer: Verify event ordering, idempotency, transaction boundaries, retry behavior, and monitoring for projection lag.
